issues.description: The build() method uses replace_in_file() to modify the 'configure' script (a generated file) at build time: replace_in_file(self, configure_script, 'umask 077', 'umask 022'). Rule R14 states that generated files (config.h, configure, Makefile.in, CMakeCache.txt) should not be modified directly and changes should go through generate() or patches/. While this configure is generated at build time by autoreconf() (not a committed file), and the task notes confirm it is a documented platform workaround for HMDFS filesystem umask 077 issue, the approach technically violates R14. Moving to generate() is not feasible because autoreconf() has not run yet at generate() time, and patching configure.ac for autoconf's internal umask behavior is complex.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider creating a patch for configure.ac or aclocal.m4 that addresses the umask behavior at the source level. Alternatively, document this as an accepted platform-specific exception in notes.md with a clear rationale for why generate()/patches/ cannot be used (autoreconf generates configure in build(), umask 077 is set by autoconf internals not configure.ac).

issues.description: Hardcoded absolute path '/storage/Users/currentUser/usr/local' is used for include/lib directories and PKG_CONFIG_PATH when self.settings.os in ('Linux', 'OHOS'). This OHOS CI-worker-specific path also applies to Linux builds where it will not exist, potentially causing compiler warnings about non-existent include/lib paths on non-CI Linux machines. The path is well-documented in comments as the location of pre-installed tools (ragel, userspace-rcu, libsodium), but hardcoding it makes the recipe non-portable.
issues.fix_suggestion: Restrict the hardcoded path to self.settings.os == 'OHOS' only (since /storage/Users/currentUser is an OHOS-specific path structure), or use an environment variable or Conan profile setting (e.g., self.options.get_safe('local_prefix')) to make the path configurable.

issues.description: test.c only prints 'test_gdnsd: OK' and returns 0 without calling any gdnsd API, which superficially matches the R34 'deception - only print without calling API' pattern. However, the actual binary test is in test_package/conanfile.py test() which runs 'gdnsd --version' and checks exit code 2. Since gdnsd is an application (package_type='application') with no library API or public headers, there is nothing for test.c to include or call. The R34 rule is satisfied by the test_package as a whole (it executes the binary).
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a more explicit comment in test.c explaining the test strategy: 'This C file only verifies CMake build/link succeeds. The actual gdnsd binary execution test is in conanfile.py test()'. Optionally, if gdnsd installs any headers, include one to verify header installation.

issues.description: patch_description fields do not start with the patch number prefix as shown in the code-style example ('0001 build aux config.guess'). The gdnsd descriptions start with descriptive text ('Guard pthread_setcanceltype...') without the numeric prefix.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider prefixing descriptions with the patch number, e.g., '0001 Guard pthread_setcanceltype with #ifdef __OHOS__ (musl libc missing pthread_cancel)'.

issues.description: commands.json includes a 'homepage' field that is not present in the standard format examples in code-style.md or review-memory.md rule 15. The standard fields are name, type, description, versions. The extra field is harmless but deviates from the documented schema.
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove the 'homepage' field to match the standard commands.json schema, or document it as an allowed optional extension in the code-style rules.

summary:
